historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (23.76%) diverges from Revenue CAGR (14.52%) by 63.6% — exceeds 30% threshold. Divergence driven by two factors: (1) strong earnings growth (18.82% EPS CAGR) building retained earnings faster than revenue growth, and (2) massive AI capex cycle compressing FCF (3.20% 3yr CAGR) well below revenue growth. Using Revenue CAGR as the primary selected rate as it best represents sustainable business growth trajectory. Equity CAGR is inflated by the earnings quality of the subscription model; FCF CAGR is temporarily depressed by $64.5B FY2025 capex. Base case growth rates set above selected rate to reflect Q3 FY2026 Azure +40% YoY momentum.

base.notes: Growth starts at 16% reflecting Q3 FY2026 run rate (+18% YoY) with modest deceleration as AI normalizes post-capacity buildout. FCF margin anchored at FY2025 actual (25.4%), assuming capex moderates from $64B peak toward $50B range by Year 4-5 so margin holds steady. WACC 10% reflects MSFT AA+ credit quality offset by elevated capex risk and regulatory overhang. Assumptions unchanged from 2026-06-30 model — no new filings since last update; July 2026 news (workforce restructuring, Xbox reset, Microsoft Frontier Company launch) is cost-discipline/AI-monetization signal, not a driver of revised revenue or margin assumptions.

bull.notes: Azure capacity constraints lift in H2 CY2026, unlocking pent-up demand and sustaining 40%+ growth. AI ARR compounds from $37B: M365 Copilot seats scale from 20M toward 100M+, GitHub Copilot monetizes 140K enterprise orgs. $627B commercial RPO converts strongly. FCF margin expands to 28% as capex stabilizes and high-margin AI services grow as a share of mix. WACC 9% reflects strong execution and credit quality. Microsoft Frontier Company (launched July 2026) is a modest incremental upside lever for higher-margin AI implementation revenue, consistent with — not additive beyond — existing bull assumptions.

bear.notes: Capex-to-revenue conversion disappoints — $190B CY2026 capex does not translate to commensurate revenue; asset impairments possible on short-lived GPU assets. Regulatory interventions (FTC antitrust, EU DMA gatekeeper designation) force licensing changes reducing Azure competitive advantage. OpenAI non-exclusive amendment erodes differentiation. FCF margin compressed to 22% by sustained high depreciation and elevated infrastructure costs per AI revenue dollar. WACC 12% reflects regulatory risk premium. July 2026 Xbox restructuring and ~4,800 layoffs are consistent with bear-case concerns about capital misallocation, though treated as cost-discipline rather than a further downgrade to bear assumptions.

probability_weighted.calculation: 0.25 * $343.97 (bull) + 0.50 * $213.37 (base) + 0.25 * $109.88 (bear) = $220.15. Weights reflect: Base as most likely given revenue trajectory and known capacity constraint resolution in H2 CY2026; Bull probability tempered by OpenAI non-exclusivity and $190B capex ROI uncertainty; Bear probability reflects non-trivial regulatory and margin compression risks.

anomalies: All three scenarios produce intrinsic values below current market price ($385.10), consistent with MSFT trading at a significant premium to DCF-derived intrinsic value. The bull case at $343.97 is now 10.7% below current price (was 6.7% below at the 2026-06-30 price of $368.57), as the stock has risen ~4.5% since the last valuation while underlying model assumptions are unchanged.
No arithmetic anomalies detected. Internal consistency verified across all four sanity check steps.

FCF margin held constant across projection years within each scenario; in practice, FCF margin will likely be suppressed in Y1-Y2 (peak capex depreciation) before recovering in Y3-Y5. This introduces slight conservatism in early years relative to true FCF trajectory.

No new financial filings since the 2026-06-30 model (still through Q3 FY2026 / quarter ended March 31, 2026); this refresh only updates the market price and derived upside/entry-discount figures. Q4 FY2026 earnings due July 29, 2026 will require a full model refresh once reported.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base-case IV of $213.37 implies 15.6x P/E on FY2025 EPS (12.7x on TTM EPS through Q3 FY2026), 4.6x P/B and 12.0x EV/EBIT — all well BELOW the 10yr historical ranges (P/E 25.4-46.3x, avg 33.7x). The DCF is conservative relative to any multiple the market has paid for MSFT in a decade; the negative upside (-44.6%) reflects the market pricing MSFT at a persistent premium to Gordon-growth DCF value, not a model error. If MSFT merely reverts to its 10yr MINIMUM P/E of 25.4x on TTM EPS ($16.80), the price would be ~$427.

notes: Live price $385.10 fetched from Yahoo Finance on 2026-07-12 (valuation date). Prior model used $368.57 (2026-06-30); stock has risen ~4.5% since then, likely reflecting a modestly positive market reaction to the Microsoft Frontier Company launch (+1.6% on announcement day) and workforce restructuring being read as cost discipline ahead of Q4 FY2026 earnings (July 29, 2026), even as the stock remains roughly 30% below its 52-week high (~$555).
Net debt is negative (-$51,414M), meaning Microsoft holds $51.4B more cash than debt. Equity value = Enterprise Value + $51,414M (net cash add-back).
Base case growth of 16% in Y1 is consistent with Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of +18% YoY and Q4 FY2026 guidance of $87.25B midpoint (+~14% YoY), implying full-year FY2026 revenue of ~$327B.

FCF was $71,611M in FY2025 despite $281,724M revenue (25.4% margin), compressed by $64,551M capex (highest in company history). FY2026 capex is guided >$120B for the fiscal year, which will further depress FCF in the near term. The model projects FCF using revenue * margin; actual FCF in Y1-Y2 may be lower if capex exceeds expectations.
Commercial RPO of $627B (+99% YoY) provides strong multi-year revenue visibility; approximately $157B expected to convert within 12 months. This backstop reduces downside risk in the base case.
AI ARR of $37B+ growing at 123% YoY is the highest-upside variable in this model. If AI ARR reaches $100B+ by FY2028, bull case assumptions would be conservative.

Sensitivity matrix uses base case growth rates with varying WACC (8-12%) and terminal growth (2-4%). At 9% WACC / 3.5% terminal growth ($267), the stock would be approximately fairly valued relative to the 2026-06-30 price; at the current $385.10 price, no cell in the sensitivity grid reaches fair value, underscoring the premium the market is now paying.

Entry price analysis: To achieve a 15% CAGR over 5 years based on each scenario's terminal value per share, entry at $123 (base), $207 (bull), or $58 (bear) would be required. Current price implies the market is paying for terminal value well above any scenario's projected terminal per-share value except for an extreme bull case.

Regulatory tail risk (FTC antitrust, EU DMA, UK CMA) is not explicitly modeled but is captured qualitatively through higher WACC in the bear case (12%). EU's mid-2026 first DMA review flagged cloud and AI as top enforcement priorities, reinforcing (but not increasing) this already-modeled risk.

The $900M Q4 FY2026 voluntary retirement charge and the subsequent ~4,800-role July 2026 layoff (2.1% of workforce, concentrated in Xbox/sales) are treated as one-time/cost-discipline items and excluded from normalized FCF margin assumptions; underlying financial statements are unchanged pending the July 29, 2026 Q4 FY2026 earnings report.
